newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India up on local gains, political hopes.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India up on local gains, political hopes.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts climbed along with the local market on Wednesday as hopes that a resolution to the country's political crisis continued to underpin sentiment, traders said.
They said direction was likely to be determined by politics ahead of Friday's confidence vote in Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's ruling coalition.
His United Front coalition held talks with the Congress Party on Wednesday, and would resume on Thursday in an attempt to ensure the government's survival.
Analysts in London said they expected a resolution to the crisis, largely because a mid-term election was not in the interests in any of the parties involved.
Also, they said it was possible that parliament would seek to pass the 1997/8 budget on Friday at the same time as the confidence vote.
Most GDR prices were higher, Hindalco collecting 30 cents to $29.25/$30.25 and SBI making 23 cents to $20.25/$21.25.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 1.82 points, or 2.51 percent, up at 74.41 points, with the premium over the local market at 18.45 percent from 19.24 percent on Tuesday.
Taiwanese GDRs extended gains, although at a slower rate than Tuesday, in an active market, traders said. They said a 2.3 percent rise in Taipei stocks had driven gains.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended 2.34 points up at 130.64, representing a discount to the local market of 4.27 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 0.23 points, or 0.35 percent, up at 64.76, a premium of 29.30 percent over the local market.
